source.title: Grokking Finite-Dimensional Algebra
source.citation: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo et al., 2026
source.authors: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo; Guillaume Dumas; Guillaume Rabusseau

record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking and representation–generalization dynamics in a new setting: multiplication in finite-dimensional algebras beyond the group tasks emphasized in the original sources.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own train/test accuracy, generalization timing, and representation-probe results. Rows below cover the textual findings and principal plotted comparisons. Exact values available only as curves or figures are recorded as figure only. Cited results and theoretical claims without new experimental outcomes are not rows.
record.test_reason: Trains MLPs (and a Transformer and LSTM) on multiplication in finite-field algebras, a new algorithmic setting. It reports train/test accuracy over steps, the grokking delay (t4−t2) and its dependence on training fraction. It also reports a representation probe tracked over training. These bear directly on V1 and partly on V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress two further findings. Unitality can lengthen grokking delays, with associative non-unital algebras grokking earliest. Lower structure-tensor rank and sparsity shorten the delay. They frame grokking over finite fields as arising from the need to form internal representations, and FDA learning over the reals as connected to low-rank matrix recovery.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random train/test partitions of finite-field algebra multiplication examples and train/test accuracy over training, close to the algorithmic grokking setup. It extends beyond group operations and uses MLP, Transformer Encoder, and LSTM models; the MLP experiments use AdamW and the specified task-specific setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that delay depends on training fraction and algebra properties; a single multiplication-rule perturbation can substantially change delay. Representation-probe results vary by architecture and layer, with the Transformer embedding layer an exception.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy increases with the algebra-consistency of layer features in low-data regimes (MLP, Transformer, LSTM). The Transformer embedding layer shows no such structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization in grokking coincides with layer features becoming linearly decodable as a bilinear map consistent with the task's algebraic structure; the layer at which this appears varies by architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Algebraic properties of the task change the grokking delay. Associative non-unital (especially commutative) algebras grok fastest. Higher rank or sparsity of the structure tensor lengthens the delay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The length of the grokking delay depends on structural properties of the target operation (unitality, commutativity, tensor rank and sparsity).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Most experiments are restricted to small algebras, especially n=2 over F7; the text acknowledges this limits empirical scope. It samples 10 tensors per category and repeats each category–tensor–training-fraction experiment twice. Many outcomes are shown only in plots, and the paper reports no null-control comparison for the grokking results.
record.rows_left_out: Exact per-curve values and additional condition-specific results in Figures 4–6 and 11–14 are not transcribed individually; the text gives the main trends but the plotted values are not available as tabled numbers. The principal algebra categories, data-fraction trend, and additional-algebra examples are represented in R2–R7.

untested.parts: Only finite-field algebras with small n and p (mostly n=2 over F7) are tested. No exact delay values are given in text; trends come from figures.
No Fourier or circuit analysis and no tracking of memorization removal. No progress measure is shown to rise before the test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data and no sweeps of initialization scale or weight norm.
Weight decay is fixed (AdamW, 0.1). There is no ungrokking test and no critical-size analysis, although small r gives memorization only.
Algorithms learned across runs are not compared.
Optimizer and numerics are fixed (AdamW, PyTorch default init); no artifact controls.

missing.what: Test loss and grokking time t4 increase with structure-tensor rank r(3) and sparsity s across r; the same holds for the other mode unfoldings.
Grokking curves for a 2-layer Transformer (r=0.5) and a 3-layer LSTM (r=0.3) on complex numbers over F7.
Phase-transition times t1–t4 as a function of r per algebra category.

record.verdict_notes: An original source for V1/V2 is not among the study's authors. The R9 probe coincides with rather than precedes the jump. Because the probe is not a circuit-based measure, this limits rather than refutes V2. The small-r memorization-only regime resembles a critical data size, but weight decay is not varied, so V5 remains untested. The figure caption calls the MLP 2-layer while the appendix calls it three-layer.

versions.untested_parts: Tests sampled finite-field algebras, not all small algorithmic datasets. The text describes the training-fraction trend but does not establish a universal quantitative law for how delay changes with training-set size.

Measures algebra-like feature alignment and its relation to test accuracy, but does not track the removal of memorizing components, test a Fourier algorithm, or establish that the probe leads the accuracy jump in time.
No experiments on non-algorithmic data or sweeps of initialization scale or weight norm.
No realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiments.
Does not test a low-norm efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not identify and compare algorithms learned across runs.
Uses AdamW and PyTorch default initialization but does not test whether optimizer or numerical choices cause or eliminate the delay.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.size_stated: The appendix states input, hidden, and output dimensions are all m2 = 28.
rows.operation_detail: Probe whether model features admit a bilinear map aligned with algebra multiplication.
rows.measure: Representation quality Arep over training steps
rows.value: figure only; text says Arep stays relatively low before grokking and then sharply increases as the model groks
rows.note: The reported probe change is sharp rather than gradual, so it does not support the gradual-formation part of V2.
rows.check: The probe stays low and then rises sharply as the model groks, coinciding with the jump rather than anticipating it. That is absence of anticipation for this probe, not a reversal. The probe (bilinear algebra-alignment of features) differs from the circuit-based measures V2 names.

relationships.condition: MLP on complex numbers over F7, sampled 2-dimensional F7 algebras across categories, M2(F3) and UT2(F5)
relationships.reason: Nontrivial delay after train accuracy saturates (R1, R6, R7). The delay persists under single-rule perturbations (R8) and across algebra categories (R3–R5). The delay shrinks as r→1 and only memorization occurs at small r (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Generalization followed training saturation across algebra categories and single-rule perturbations, with shorter delays as the training fraction approached one and only memorization at small fractions.
